name: Yusuf Weber

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal workday look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I teach beginner piano on Mondays, play with the supper-club band on Thursdays and sell small demo tracks to singers. I finished secondary school and still need the band leader to catch me if I rush a turn.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What makes the day good, and what takes effort?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I like a singer leaning into a phrase and the band following without a word. The hard part is a club call time that changes after we arrange the children’s pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the supper club that AI making the booking list quicker is useful. The piano still needs someone to hear when the singer wants another bar.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We have about ten months of expenses saved and my partner’s paramedic salary is steady. I am a junior pianist in the club band, but a lost Thursday set would not threaten the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep Thursday club sets and Monday beginner piano pupils this season. I already use AI every day to draft practice tracks, and I check the rhythm at the keyboard before pupils hear them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about this picture. The home budget can take one missed date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened when the club shut for a storm?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The last storm shut the club for one night and the owner paid half the fee. I would ask for that term in writing before the next winter season.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does your son see you practise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My son hears me repeat a run until my hand stops rushing. He calls it boring, but he likes the finished tune.

I would ask for a **written storm fee** before winter.
think: Our **ten-month cushion** and paramedic pay secure the mortgage after one lost set.
I still rely on **piano pupils** to keep my own earnings steady.
do: Keep **Thursday club sets** and Monday piano pupils this season.
Ask the club owner for a **written storm fee** before winter.
feel: I feel **calm** because one lost date fits the budget.
S0.quote: The piano still needs someone to hear when the singer wants another bar.
fieldNote: His **strong savings** and partner’s paramedic pay make one missed club night manageable.
Daily **AI practice tracks** are existing use and checked at his own keyboard.

steps.text: Keep Thursday supper-club piano sets and Monday beginner pupils

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the club owner that AI may answer bookings, write posters and make backing tracks, but the band needs a clear fee. I would ask for the next quarter in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The little piano demos I sell to singers could lose buyers, roughly a sixth of a good month. The club might book fewer live sets too, although that has not happened yet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would ask for a signed quarter of Thursday dates and test one new AI audio-cleanup tool after the sound technician demonstrates it. In the first year I would use only my own demo, compare the cleaned file with the original by ear and stop if it changes a note.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious about my demo income even with savings. I can test a tool, but I cannot make a singer buy a track.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Whose audio would you use to test the cleaner?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not put a pupil’s voice into a service without permission or a clear storage rule. If the club wants that, I would use my own recording first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What minimum number of club sets would you ask for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the owner for two paid sets a month at minimum. If the offer has only one, I would teach the existing pupils and ask a nearby venue about posted dates.

I would tell the owner that **live fees** still matter beside backing tracks.

do: Request a **signed club quarter** next month with two paid sets monthly.
Test an **AI audio cleaner** on my own demo after technician proof, compare by ear and stop if notes change.

feel: I feel **anxious** about possible demo losses despite the reserve.
S1.quote: I can test a tool, but I cannot make a singer buy a track.
fieldNote: His new **audio trial** uses his own file, a technician’s demonstration and a listening stop rule.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the club that AGI by 2028 could make demo tracks for nothing, but a singer still needs a live accompanist. I would ask for the paid Thursday dates before agreeing to rehearse.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my demo sales to end in 2028, and the club may try generated music too. Robots that can play hands-on parts follow around 2031, so live piano gets a few more years, but I cannot count on every date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask for the signed club schedule and call two nearby venues about advertised paid piano sets. If 2028 AGI cuts our Thursdays, I would apply only where the written net fee after travel beats my current lost pay and the hours fit school pickup; I would keep Monday pupils until a contract is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious about losing my demos and perhaps club dates. The gap in my own piano earnings would be real, even with ten months saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much of the reserve would you keep untouched?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would leave six months of household expenses untouched while testing venues. I would not pay a deposit on an unsigned show.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could the paramedic shift cover every pickup?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner can do pickup on early shifts but not every Thursday. I would choose a venue whose actual call time fits the children’s school day.

say: I would ask for **signed paid Thursdays** before rehearsing.
I would defend **live accompaniment** even when demos become cheap.
think: My **demo sales** likely end in 2028 before 2031 playing robots.
The club may also cut **Thursday dates** before robots arrive.
do: Ask for the **signed club schedule** and two posted venue options this week.
Apply for **advertised paid sets** after 2028 cuts only if net travel pay beats lost fees and pickup fits.
Avoid **show deposits** until a contract is signed, keeping six months of savings untouched.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my own lost income, with time to search.
S2.quote: The gap in my own piano earnings would be real, even with ten months saved.
fieldNote: He separates **2028 demo loss** from later 2031 robot performance.
The venue move needs **posted paid work** and written net pay above lost fees, plus pickup fit.

steps.text: Apply for posted piano sets if 2028 dates fall, net pay rises and pickup fits
Keep Monday pupils until a new venue contract is signed

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the club that AGI by 2031 gives us five years to build an audience that asks for us by name. I would propose a paid early supper set if the owner can show enough bookings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My demos probably end by 2031, but a regular early set might replace them. Robots around 2034 could play piano parts, though I cannot tell what guests will want beside dinner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This autumn I would offer one early supper set on a trial date only if the owner guarantees a written fee and a finish before child pickup. If the trial draws at least twenty paying tables, I would ask for a four-date contract; in the first year after 2031 I would keep those dates only while the net fee covers travel and a babysitter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious until that new set pays. Five years gives me time to build a paid supper set, not count unsigned tables.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why twenty paying tables?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Twenty tables is the owner’s number for an extra band. If we draw twelve, I would keep the current Thursday set and not ask players to work a free second night.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you advertise without misleading guests?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use AI to draft the poster, then ask the owner to check the meal details before printing. I would never send a fake picture of a full room.

I would refuse a **free second night** for the band.
think: My **demo sales** may end by 2031 before 2034 stage robots.

feel: I feel **anxious** until the new paid set proves itself.
S3.quote: Five years gives me time to build a paid supper set, not count unsigned tables.
fieldNote: The new set needs a **written fee** and a finish before child pickup for the first trial.

steps.text: Trial early supper set only with written fee and finish before pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children that AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to learn useful tools and keep honest stage work. I would still play paid club sets while the owner books us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2036 the early supper set might pay more than demos did if guests return. Robots around 2039 could play piano, but our current pupils, partner pay and savings protect the next few years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I would save half of each paid demo fee after bills until the reserve reaches twelve months. In the first year after 2036 I would compare actual club and lesson pay, and take a posted paid venue offer only if current dates fall, written net pay after travel improves and pickup fits.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would feel uneasy about stage work far ahead. The mortgage is covered now, and I have time to see which paid sets last.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you save after demo sales stop?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Twelve months is a goal, not cash I already have. If demos stop early, I would save from paid lessons only after food and mortgage are covered, leaving six months untouched.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you teach your children about pay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children that a good player sends a clear invoice and pays the band. A full room is not enough if a drummer goes home unpaid.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because demos may vanish before club dates are signed. Written Thursdays, posted paid venues with better net fees and a six-month savings floor would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask whether the last player is paid when a show runs late. A singer can stretch a phrase only when the band listens together.

headlineQuote: A singer can stretch a phrase only when the band listens together.
portrait: At **43**, Yusuf is a junior pianist with secondary school education, two children, a mortgage and ten months saved.
His partner’s **paramedic salary** steadies the household while demos and club dates remain exposed.
He uses **AI daily** but trials a new audio cleaner only on his own file with technician proof and listening checks.
He seeks **written net fees** and real paid tables before adding sets, while saving actual demo income toward twelve months.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** may erase demo sales before Yusuf knows whether club Thursdays remain paid.
whatWouldHelp: **Written paid dates**, better net venue offers and a six-month reserve would let Yusuf test other work.
